correctness.rationale: Derived exactly from pivot-invariant independent Gaussian polar coordinates. Reinforcing sign probability 1/2, two angular constraints and Rayleigh radius ratio yield the exact 2D probability; differentiate F_c to obtain the 1D quadrature. Uniform endpoint Taylor expansions over a triangular shrinking domain give delta^2/(2*pi^2)+O(delta^3). Independent 1D and 2D quadratures and Monte Carlo were executed from CHECK.py; simulations do not establish the proof.

originality.rationale: Claim-level comparisons with six primary papers distinguish deterministic upper bounds, approximate mean growth, general-n probabilistic bounds, and structured butterfly distributions from the complete iid Gaussian 2x2 survival law and exact endpoint coefficient. Targeted semantic and web searches did not find a covering theorem; a plausible inaccessible older technical report remains a disclosed bibliographic risk. This is a best-knowledge judgment, not proof of uniqueness.
residual_risks: D. Macleod, historical unpublished 1988 technical report on the distribution of GEPP growth could not be obtained; exact two-dimensional calculations in it are unknown.
Not every appendix and unrelated section of every lengthy source was inspected; equivalent unindexed derivations remain possible.
Semantic and keyword searches cannot prove mathematical uniqueness.

value.rationale: Complete exact law for the smallest nontrivial Gaussian GEPP problem resolves all thresholds including an atypical atom at one and sharp rare-event tail probability near the worst deterministic bound. It is a reproducible analytic base-case benchmark for ongoing random-elimination stability and rare growth studies, not an arbitrary slice or a routine numerical table lookup.
